extracted.intended_audience: public relations practitioners, measurement and research professionals, agencies, clients and industry stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A press release announcing a new industry coalition to develop standards and best practices for public relations research, measurement and evaluation, describing scope, partners, process and goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices, common definitions and measurement standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry practitioners should develop, recommend and apply best practices, common definitions and measurement standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance: “We know that clients, both external and internal, are asking for industry practitioners to develop, recommend and apply best practices, common definitions and measurement standards.” The press release frames this as a principal objective for the coalition to meet client expectations and avoid external imposition of standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master framework applicable across PR activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a master framework that can be applied across public relations activities including traditional media relations, corporate communications and social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The standards platform will provide a master framework that can be applied across PR activities; explicit examples listed: traditional media relations, corporate communications and social media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder inclusion (clients, agencies, research providers, thought leaders)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards development should bring together the views of clients, agencies, research providers and thought leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coalition will bring together the views of clients, agencies, research providers and thought leaders to ensure the platform reflects multiple constituent perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent measurement processes regardless of topic or communication vehicle
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide consistent measurement processes regardless of the topic or type of communication vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: “The coalition seeks to bring all of that together to provide consistent measurement processes regardless of the topic or type of communication vehicle.” Emphasis on process consistency across topics and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow ISO procedures for consensus on voluntary industry-wide standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards development work will follow procedures recommended by the International Standards Organization for developing consensus on voluntary industry-wide standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The coalition will build working groups and develop recommendations following ISO-recommended procedures, indicating a desire for recognized consensus-building methodology and voluntary (not regulatory) adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify specific areas in need of standards and form working groups
rubrics_metrics.description: The coalition will identify specific areas in need of standards and best practices, and build working groups to develop recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance: targeted gap identification followed by focused working groups to produce recommendations; indicates an iterative, topic-by-topic development process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universally accepted measures to gauge performance of communications programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop universally accepted measures to gauge the performance of communications programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted objective: “Creating universally accepted measures to gauge the performance of communications programs will be an important part of our industry’s continued growth.” Emphasis on broad acceptance and ability to assess program performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards should facilitate comparative evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards should facilitate comparative evaluation of individual programs and specific program elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: “Standards facilitate comparative evaluation of individual programs and specific program elements.” Practical purpose: enable benchmarking and comparison across programs/elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonize definitions and methods so professionals can focus on design and insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonize definitions and methods, allowing research professionals to focus on research, measurement and evaluation design, and delivering critical insights to clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted rationale: “Standards also harmonize definitions and methods, allowing research professionals to focus instead on research, measurement and evaluation design, and delivering critical insights to clients.” Emphasizes reducing methodological confusion so practitioners can concentrate on analysis and insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive industry-led standard setting to avoid external imposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Industry should proactively develop standards because clients and purchasing departments may impose requirements if the industry does not self-regulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted warning: “If we do not do this ourselves, be prepared for clients and their purchasing departments to do it for us.” Implies criterion that standards work should be timely and industry-led.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise standards and share knowledge as core aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards development should raise industry standards and promote sharing of knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: “Raising standards and sharing knowledge are fundamental to the Global Alliance’s mission,” linking standards work to professional development and knowledge dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary, industry-wide (non-regulatory) orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: The standards are intended to be voluntary industry-wide standards rather than regulatory mandates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press release repeatedly frames the platform as voluntary and industry-driven, with consensus-based development and broad adoption as objectives rather than legal compulsion.
